subject: RFI: Predictable tail-latency budgeting & GPU blend for Phoenix Health Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit.patel@phoenixhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Cho <lauren.cho@phoenixhealth.com>, procurement@phoenixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFI: Predictable tail-latency budgeting & GPU blend for Dedicated pool

Hi Soojin / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking this RFI — Phoenix Health is evaluating a reserved inference pool for several interactive and background LLM features across our patient engagement products. Attached is our questionnaire and a small sample of production traffic (anon) to help baseline. Key asks:

- Can Redwood propose a GPU mix (by instance type) that meets our P99.9 tail-latency SLO for interactive flows while minimizing committed spend?
- What reservation % do you recommend versus keeping burst on-demand?
- Any constraints around quantization/precision that would materially affect quality for our medical-lexicon prompts?

We'd like an initial sizing note and a short workbook estimate by EOD Thursday if possible.

Attachments: Phoenix_RFI_Attach.pdf (questionnaire)

Thanks,
Amit Patel
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
Phoenix Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit.patel@phoenixhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Predictable tail-latency budgeting & GPU blend for Dedicated pool

Amit — thanks for the brief and the sample. We'll take this on. I've looped in Marcus (capacity modeling) and Rishi (SLA/pricing) to coordinate a short response pack.

Quick clarifying questions so we size sensibly:
1) Which model families do you intend to serve from the reserved pool (e.g., Llama-2-70B, open-weight 65B variants, or custom fine-tuned checkpoints)?
2) Is the 99.9% SLO referenced strictly for the interactive patient chat flows, or do you want the same for batch/background workflows?
3) Any hard constraints on quantization (i.e., is INT8/4 acceptable, or do you require FP16 for production quality checks)?
4) Can you confirm expected token distributions (typical/long tail) — the sample helps, but we prefer an explicit percent split if available.

We'll produce a short workbook with two reservation scenarios (conservative vs cost-optimized) and recommended GPU families. Expect a first pass by 2026-12-03. Sharing our brief cover note and runbook link now.

Attachment: redwood_rfi_cover_note.pdf

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: RFI: Predictable tail-latency budgeting & GPU blend for Dedicated pool

Hi Soojin / Redwood — thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline below and attaching a small anonymized CSV (phoenix-workload-sample.csv):

1) Models: primary is a fine-tuned Llama-2 family (~70B-family weights), with an occasional smaller 13B variant used for lower latency notifications.
2) SLOs: P99.9 target is 350ms for interactive patient chat (web/mobile). Background workflows (batch summarization, nightly indexing) can tolerate up to 1s.
3) Quantization: We are open to INT8 for the 70B family if you can demonstrate parity on clinical QA prompts — otherwise FP16.
4) Token distribution (approx): 70% <= 64 tokens; 20% 65–256 tokens; 10% 257–1024 tokens.
5) Traffic shape: baseline steady-state ~20 qps, but weekly peaks up to 140 qps (short bursts ~10–15 minutes).
6) Compliance: Data must remain in US regions; SOC2 evidence will be requested during procurement.

Please let us know assumptions you make around batching windows and cold-start behavior.

Cheers,
Lauren Cho
Product Ops, Phoenix Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Cho <lauren.cho@phoenixhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Predictable tail-latency budgeting & GPU blend for Dedicated pool

Lauren / Amit — based on the sample and your clarifications, here's a concise recommended approach (first-pass):

Assumptions used
- Model family: Llama-2 70B-like transformer (FP16/INT8 path available).
- Typical request length: median 48 tokens, 90th pct ~220 tokens, tail to 1024 tokens.
- Workload: baseline 20 qps, peak burst 140 qps (10–15m bursts).
- Target interactive SLO: P99.9 <= 350ms (interactive traffic only).

Sizing recommendation (cost-balanced):
- Reserved pool: 8 x H100-80GB + 12 x A100-80GB.
  - Expected effective steady throughput (conservative estimate with batching & KV cache): H100 ~30 qps@median (512-token budget), A100 ~18 qps@median.
  - Combined conservative headroom: 8*30 + 12*18 = 240 + 216 = 456 qps theoretical. This provides buffer for burst windows while allowing aggressive batching during steady state.

Reservation strategy
- Commit 60% of expected monthly average: keeps committed cost sensible while avoiding large overprovisioning.
- Leave 40% as on-demand bursting (hosted pool) to handle 10–15 minute spikes.

Quality guardrails and quantization
- We recommend a staged INT8 trial for the 70B family: run A/B QA across clinical prompts in a canary environment; if QA delta < 1% on your clinical metrics, adopt INT8 for 70B to reduce per-token cost by ~25–35%.
- For strict clinical flows, designate a small FP16 subset of GPUs (A100) for gold-path hedging.

Operational notes
- Tail-latency: to meet P99.9@350ms you should (a) enable short batching windows for interactive route, (b) provision local KV caching for warmed sessions, and (c) use pre-warming for scheduled spikes where possible.
- Canary & rollout: start with a 2-week canary (10% traffic) on the reserved pool, measure P99/P99.9 across the prompt set, then widen to 50% and full cutover.

Deliverables we will send by COB Monday:
- A single-page workbook with conservative and cost-optimized reservation sheets (drive link).
- Per-GPU throughput curves and tail-latency estimates for your sample traffic.
- A suggested procurement commitment schedule and fallback policy template (canary/A-B).

Next steps
1) Schedule a 30–45m sizing session (we have availability Mon/Tue next week) to walk through the workbook live.
2) If acceptable, we'll prepare a formal reservation term sheet and pricing options (12/24/36 month).

Attachments referenced: phoenix-workload-sample.csv
Shared links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPHX-sizing-workbook

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference
